<action type="say">
My system isn’t showing any emergency plumbers I can book directly in your area, so let’s (1) stop damage and (2) get you ready to call local 24/7 plumbers immediately.

1) Shut the water off (as much as possible)
- Under the kitchen sink: look for two small valves on the pipes going up to the faucet (hot and cold).  
  - Turn **both valves clockwise** until they stop.  
- If you don’t see valves or they won’t move, use the **main shutoff**:
  - Often in the garage, on an outside wall near where water enters the house, or in a ground box near the street.
  - Turn the main valve **clockwise** (or 90° if it’s a lever) to shut water to the whole house.
- Put a **bucket or pan** under the leak and **towels** inside the cabinet and on the floor to protect it.

2) While that’s stabilizing, find a plumber to come today
On your phone, open Google/Maps and search:
- “24 hour plumber near me” or  
- “emergency plumber Fort Worth 76102”

Pick 2–3 with:
- Good ratings (ideally 4.0+), and  
- “24/7” or “emergency service” in the listing.

3) What to say when you call
Use this script (you can read it off):

“I’m at **1234 Main Street, Fort Worth, TX 76102**. My **kitchen sink is leaking under the cabinet** and it **drips even when the faucet is off**. I’ve **shut off the water under the sink / at the main** (or: I **haven’t been able to shut it off yet**). How soon can someone get here **today**, and what is your **service call fee** and **hourly rate**, including any **emergency/after-hours charges**?”

Ask each plumber:
- Soonest **arrival time** today.  
- **Service call / trip fee** and whether it’s applied to the repair.  
- **Hourly rate** and any **emergency surcharge**.  
- Confirm they’re **licensed and insured in Texas**.

If you can safely peek in the cabinet and tell me:
- Where the water seems to come from (pipe/trap vs. flexible lines vs. back of cabinet), and  
- Whether you managed to shut the water off fully,

I can give you a quick idea of what’s likely wrong and a rough cost range so you know what to expect when they quote you. </action>
